hero.intro: Getting a hansgrohe shower valve or basin mixer to perform properly comes down to three things at fitting stage: the water pressure it's being fed, how deep the valve body sits behind the finished wall, and whether that body was correctly positioned before the wall ever closed up. None of that changes much between one hansgrohe installation and the next, because the engineering across the range is consistent — which is exactly why getting the rough-in detail right the first time matters more than the brand name on the trim plate. We work fit-only across Gerrards Cross, the Buckinghamshire commuter village around 25 to 30 minutes from our Bracknell base: you source the hansgrohe shower system, basin mixer and whatever sanitaryware it's paired with — often Duravit, Villeroy & Boch or Laufen — through your showroom or designer, and we strip out, first-fix, tile, plumb and snag it from £3,500. Because the valve body position is fixed before any tiling goes on, confirming exactly what's specified at survey — rather than after the wall has closed up — is where a Gerrards Cross hansgrohe project actually gets decided.

sections.heading: Rough-in depth: the detail that can't be corrected later
sections.body: A hansgrohe valve body is set once, behind the final tiled finish, and it isn't something that can be adjusted after the wall has closed up without opening it back up again. Getting the rough-in depth right means knowing the finished tile thickness before the valve body goes in, not after — a detail that's easy to get wrong if the tiling and plumbing aren't sequenced and confirmed together at first fix. Alongside rough-in depth, we check the water pressure feeding the system against what the specified hansgrohe product needs, and confirm the valve body position is correctly set before any boarding or tiling goes over it. None of this changes because of which hansgrohe product has been specified — the engineering is consistent across the range — which is exactly why the fitting sequence and confirmation at survey matter more than the product itself.
